review_notes: I read the whole file and checked the Mathlib API in Mathlib/RingTheory/LocalRing/Pullback.lean. That file has pullbackFst/pullbackSnd but no swap isomorphism, so the fst/snd symmetry can't be removed by transport. Instead I propose one generic lemma over a ring map φ : A →+* B, an ideal K of A and an ideal J of B. The proposals are untested: I could not compile Lean, and I did not write out the exact generic statements or check them against the Mathlib API. The `_g` and `_f` placeholder arguments of fstSource and sndSource, and the definitional unfolding of fstMap into Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom _), would need checking when the change is made. The ker_fst_mul_ker_snd / ker_toBase / target lattice lemmas are not duplicated in a way that would justify a shared lemma.

findings.problem: The two ~58-line proofs are the same argument with fst/snd, ker f/ker g and (a,0)/(0,a) swapped. Both pick a ∈ ker f with a ∉ x, build b, and take V = basicOpen b. They then deduce injectivity from the isomorphism of the restriction fstMap ∣_ V, and build the cover W = φ⁻¹ V with i = homOfLE. Finally they rewrite via morphismRestrict_ι. This is real topological and scheme-theoretic reasoning, and any fix to one copy has to be repeated in the other.
findings.proposed_change: Add one private lemma for a ring map φ : A →+* B with ideals K ≤ A and J ≤ B. Its hypotheses are: (hJ) ∀ b ∈ J, φ b ∈ K; (hK) ∀ a ∈ K, ∃ b ∈ J, φ b = a; and (hbij) ∀ b ∈ J, Function.Bijective (Localization.awayMap φ b). Its conclusion is IsOpenImmersion ((kernel-style open U_K := (zeroLocus K)ᶜ).ι ≫ Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom φ)). The proof sketch is as follows. For a prime x ∈ U_K, choose a ∈ K \ x and then b ∈ J with φ b = a. The chart Spec.map φ ∣_ basicOpen b is an isomorphism because of hbij. It gives injectivity through isOpenEmbedding.injective, and gives the source cover W = φ⁻¹ basicOpen b ≤ U_K by hJ. Then `isOpenImmersion_fstOpenMap` is the lemma with K = ker f, J = ker (f.pullbackSnd g), hK a := ⟨(a,0),_⟩, hJ b := the existing hbf calc, and hbij := awayMap_fst_bijective. The snd case is the same with ⟨(0,a),_⟩. Each theorem then shrinks to a few lines.
findings.benefit: This removes about 60 lines of duplicated scheme-level proof. The pullback-specific content is reduced to three small algebraic hypotheses. The generic lemma states the real mechanism: a ring map is an open immersion on the complement of K if each element of K is hit by an element of J that gives a localization isomorphism.

findings.problem: The two range proofs repeat the same argument. In one direction, take b = (a,0) or (0,a) and show it lies in the opposite kernel. In the other, choose b in the opposite kernel with b ∉ p, invert the chart isomorphism on basicOpen b, and use morphismRestrict_base_coe plus inv_hom_apply to show the preimage point maps to p.
findings.proposed_change: Include the range statement in the generic lemma above: Set.range (ι ≫ Spec.map φ) = (zeroLocus J)ᶜ under the same hypotheses hJ, hK and hbij. The chart-inversion step is proved once, with b ∈ J, p ∉ V(J) and z := inv (Spec.map φ ∣_ basicOpen b) ⟨p,_⟩. The forward direction uses hK together with the fact that (a ∉ x and φ b = a) gives J ⊄ image prime. Both range theorems then follow by instantiating K and J as for the open immersion. The two instantiations should share their hypotheses through small local `have`s or a bundled structure.
findings.benefit: The inversion/point-chasing proof is the least pleasant part of the file. Having it once makes it much easier to read and maintain, and keeps the open-immersion and range statements in sync.

findings.problem: fst_chart_iso and snd_chart_iso differ only in which projection is used. Each turns bijectivity of Localization.awayMap into IsIso of the restriction to basicOpen b, via isIso_iff_bijective and SpecMapRestrictBasicOpenIso. Likewise fst_chart_le and snd_chart_le repeat the same argument. Both show that b has image outside the prime and b's image is killed by f (resp. g), so the preimage lies in the kernel complement.
findings.proposed_change: State these once for a generic φ : A →+* B and b : B. The first lemma says that Function.Bijective (Localization.awayMap φ b) implies IsIso (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom φ) ∣_ PrimeSpectrum.basicOpen b). The second says that if φ b ∈ K, then (Spec.map (ofHom φ)) ⁻¹ᵁ basicOpen b ≤ (zeroLocus K)ᶜ. fst_chart_* and snd_chart_* become one-line instantiations, or are inlined into the generic open-immersion lemma.
findings.benefit: This removes four near-copies and puts the chart facts in the form that the generic open-immersion and range lemmas need.

findings.problem: Both proofs repeat the same argument: injectivity via awayMap_injective_iff with witness exponent 1 and b * a = 0, and surjectivity via awayMap_surjective_iff with the preimage ⟨(b.1.1 * a, 0), _⟩ (resp. ⟨(0, b.1.2 * a), _⟩). They differ only by swapping the two coordinates. Each proof also recomputes hbf/hbg and the Subtype.ext/Prod.ext computation.
findings.proposed_change: Prove one lemma that is symmetric in the coordinates, or prove the snd version from the fst one by transporting along a ring isomorphism f.pullback g ≃+* g.pullback f (e.g. the swap). Mathlib does not appear to have this swap iso, so it would need to be defined here. Alternatively, extract the projection-agnostic fact. If b ∈ ker (pullbackSnd) and φ = pullbackFst, then φ is injective on elements a with φ a = 0 after multiplication by b. Every element b·(a,0)-type is hit. The first form is cleaner, but is more work than the generic lemma in the first finding.
findings.benefit: This halves the algebraic core (about 55 lines to about 30), and makes the left/right asymmetry explicit rather than copy-pasted. The swap iso, if introduced, would also let the open immersion, range and target theorems be derived by symmetry.
